clinician.final_diagnosis: A pathological diagnosis of post-auricular mature cystic teratoma was therefore made.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A term baby presented with a post-auricular swelling noted soon after delivery, which gradually increased in size and produced foul-smelling pus-like discharge. At 15 days of age, physical examination revealed a large (12x18 cm) lobulated mass, cystic superiorly and firm inferiorly. Laboratory tests at 15 days showed elevated WBC, neutrophilia, low hemoglobin, very high CRP, and a very high alfa-fetoprotein level. Cranial ultrasound showed Arnold–Chiari malformations grade 1 and echocardiography revealed a moderate atrial septal defect. At 30 days of age, brain MRI and CT angiography showed a mixed type of teratoma with erosion of the parietal and temporal bones. Histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis, showing a tissue section with various mature components including skin, cysts lined by cuboidal epithelium, epithelial glands, respiratory epithelium with mucus-secreting cells, mature adipose tissue, nerve tissue, and blood vessels, along with lymphocytic infiltrates.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Swelling at posterior right ear noted soon after delivery, increasing in size with foul-smelling pus-like discharge.
Physical examination at 15 days revealed a large (12x18 cm) lobulated mass, cystic superiorly and firm inferiorly, mobile, with hyperpigmentation.
Elevated inflammatory markers (WBC, CRP) and very high alfa-fetoprotein (7390.5 ng/L) at 15 days of age.
Brain MRI and CT angiography at 30 days showed a mixed type of teratoma with erosion of parietal and temporal bones.

Histopathological analysis confirmed a tissue section with mature components including skin, cysts, epithelial glands, respiratory epithelium, adipose tissue, nerve tissue, and blood vessels, consistent with mature cystic teratoma.
